title: CXCL4-induced PBMCs in extracellular vesicle-mediated vascular calcification and extracellular matrix modulation
summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate the role of monocytes, a white blood cell population involved in the immune response, in the genesis and growth of calcium depositions in the blood vessel wall, a process called atherosclerosis. This disease process is the underlying cause of heart attacks and strokes, making the mechanisms involved relevant to develop new, improved therapies. Monocytes migrate from the blood into the blood vessel wall, develop into a cell type called macrophage, and mediate specific effects depending their surrounding milieu. Through a specific stimulus termed platelet factor 4 (PF-4), migrating monocytes differentiate into so called 'M4' macrophages, whose role in the development of blood vessel calcifications is unclear to date. Previous studies have hinted at a connection between M4 macrophages and unstable atherosclerotic plaques, which are associated with an increased risk of heart attack or stroke. The mechanism through which this effect may be mediated is unknown. 
Thus, the objective of this study is to analyze the effect of M4 monocytes/macrophages on calcification of blood vessels. The investigation of the signalling pathways involved in these mechanisms are of particular interest. One potential mechanism implicated in the M4 monocyte/macrophage may be the release of specific nanoparticles called extracellular vesicles contributing to calcification. The results of this study may contribute to the discovery of new pathways in atherosclerosis with the potential for new preventative therapies, ideally lowering the risk for heart attacks or strokes in high-risk populations.

interventions.name: Healthy blood donors, from whom up to 200 ml of whole blood is drawn following written informed consent.
